statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 5 of 100 in the low band, twenty points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure removes the price path that this score measures. Stress is 59 in the elevated band on an unresolved Saudi East-West pipeline outage, crude near 100 dollars and a Wednesday policy decision priced for an increase. Confidence is 86 on a complete verified closing set.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD, and the single shared reading applies to each instrument. Two independent facts support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, yet finished 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range, while NQ futures traded down to 29,040.50 after the inflation print and recovered to settle 29,391.75, a round trip of roughly 459 points that retraced rather than extended. Second, CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, twenty-two hours after this horizon ends, so all twenty-four forecast slots describe a closed market in which a persistent no-retracement path cannot form. No evidence-based danger window is published, because a halted contract cannot define one. Stress remains elevated and is described here as an environment reading only: it does not alter the mapped state.
headline: A shut tape into the weekend: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44 and 0.91% higher but mid-range, NQ retraced a 459-point round trip after firm core CPI, VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84, and an unresolved Saudi pipeline outage plus Monday's Gulf-Iran Hormuz meeting travel toward a Sunday reopen that lies beyond this window.
body:
Friday's price path is complete and it granted retracement. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close. The cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished 105 points below the high, so the closing auction neither extended the advance nor broke it. NQ futures were wider and more instructive: a 29,040.50 low after the 12:30 UTC inflation print gave way to a 29,499.50 high and a 29,391.75 settle, a round trip in which mean reversion worked in both directions. The broader tape agreed, with the Dow up 0.98% to 52,573.29, the S&P 500 up 0.86% to 7,656.98 and the Nasdaq Composite up 0.96% to 26,333.04, each snapping a four-day losing streak. VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84, closing near the low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range, and participation was broad rather than narrow: seven of eight tracked megacaps and five of seven large semiconductors closed higher, with Arm, Qualcomm and Intel leading while Nvidia and Micron finished marginally lower.

The macro backdrop is the source of the elevated Stress reading. August CPI rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% on the year, with core at 0.3% and 2.4%; the firm core print lifted pricing for a 25 basis point increase at Wednesday's FOMC decision to roughly 85 to 90 percent, with a second move priced by year end. The 2-year yield rose about 4 basis points to roughly 4.63% and the 10-year to about 4.97%, so rates and equities moved in mild conflict rather than in one-way alignment. Energy remains the unresolved thread: Saudi Arabia shut its East-West pipeline, roughly 7 million barrels per day of capacity, after drone strikes on pump stations, while WTI still eased 2.37% to 100.05 dollars and Brent 2.81% to 104.61 on reports that Gulf foreign ministers may meet Iran's foreign minister in Oman on Monday to discuss shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

That combination defines the weekend: a completed, orderly, two-way price path behind, and a stack of unresolved supply and policy questions ahead of a reopen that this horizon does not reach. Tail therefore stays at a structural floor and rises only to 8 in the final slots as unpriced information accumulates, while Stress traces a shallow valley before firming toward the reopen and Confidence decays slowly with distance from the last observed quote.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 01:00 UTC on 11 September to 00:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at Tail 12 in mixed mode and eases to 11 through the Asian session, then firms into a trend-up read between 06:00 and 11:00 UTC as European hours extended the advance, with Tail between 13 and 15. The 12:30 UTC inflation release marks the only departure from the low band: the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC slots were published at Tail 21 and 22 in event/whipsaw mode, mapping to WATCH and a yellow status, with Confidence cut to 70 and 80 while the two-way reaction resolved. From 14:00 UTC the assessment returned to the low band in mixed mode near Tail 15 to 17, and the final four slots step down to 13, 7, 6 and 5 in normal mode as the cash close passed and the futures halt removed the price path. Stress declined steadily across the window, from the mid-80s before the release to 60 in the closing slot, as realized volatility decayed and the event risk that had dominated the session was resolved rather than extended.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, twenty-two hours after this horizon ends. Conditional Tail opens at 5 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, holds that residual floor through the overnight and Saturday European hours, then steps to 6 from 08:00 UTC, 7 from 14:00 UTC and 8 from 20:00 UTC as the stock of unpriced weekend information grows toward a reopen that still lies beyond the window. The maximum forecast value of 8 remains seventeen points below the 25-point block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON and green in all twenty-four slots and no danger window is published. Stress traces a shallow valley, easing from 59 to 56 through the dead hours as Friday's realized volatility decays, then firming to 62 in the final slot on the unresolved pipeline outage, Monday's reported Gulf-Iran meeting on Hormuz shipping and Wednesday's multi-stage policy sequence. Confidence decays slowly from 86 to 80, a function of distance from the last observed quote rather than any weakening of the verified closing evidence set.
